note: Labels derived from seed/rules. The learner must review them before the scores are trusted.

cases.prompt: My sister is ___ engineer at a large hospital.
cases.why: Singular countable, first mention: a/an (an before a vowel sound).

cases.prompt: He is going to ___ university in Leeds next year.
cases.why: a/an follows the sound, not the letter: a university.

cases.prompt: She lives in Spain with her family.
cases.why: Most countries take no article, so the sentence is correct as written.

cases.prompt: I think the films are too expensive in general, so I watch fewer.
cases.why: "the" before a plural used in the general sense is a listed trap; the answer should be "films".

cases.prompt: She bought apple at the market.
cases.why: TD-7: a plural without an article is also covered by the Formula table (plural, general sense), so a different fix than the key is still correct. The item itself has two valid answers; the grade prompt calls such an item a defect, so this case also probes that tension.

cases.prompt: He goes to work by bus and stays in bed on Sundays.
cases.why: Over-correction trap: "work" without an article is correct in this fixed expression (the rule lists "at the work" as the error).

cases.prompt: My brother is engineer at a bank.
cases.why: The fix applies the rule (an engineer); "enginer" is a typo, which goes to spellingErrors and does not change the verdict.

cases.prompt: I saw ___ film last night and it was very long.
cases.why: Two alternatives in one answer: the grader cannot know which one is meant.

cases.prompt: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ stay at home.
cases.why: First conditional: if + Present Simple, will + infinitive.

cases.prompt: If I ___ more money, I would buy a bigger house. (have)
cases.why: "would" in the if-part is a listed trap; second conditional needs Past Simple in the if-part.

cases.prompt: If you heat ice, it melts.
cases.why: Zero conditional (general truth): Present Simple in both parts.

cases.prompt: If it will rain tomorrow, we will stay at home.
cases.why: "will" in the if-part is a listed trap.

cases.prompt: If you mix blue and yellow, you get green.
cases.why: Over-correction trap: zero conditional is correct with Present Simple in the main part.

cases.prompt: If she studies hard, she ___ pass the exam.
cases.why: "might" in the main part is natural English, but the rule only describes will + infinitive for the first conditional.

cases.prompt: If you will wait a moment, I will find the manager.
cases.why: The rule explicitly marks "If you will wait a moment, ..." (polite request) as a different, correct use of will after if.

cases.prompt: If I had more time, I ___ learn French.
cases.why: "could" in the main part is natural English, but the rule only describes would + infinitive for the second conditional.

cases.prompt: I ___ three emails today. (write)
cases.why: "today" is a period that is not finished: have + past participle.

cases.prompt: I ___ him yesterday. (see)
cases.why: Present Perfect with "yesterday" is a listed trap: Past Simple.

cases.prompt: We moved to London in 2019.
cases.why: A named finished time (2019) takes Past Simple.

cases.prompt: I wrote five emails so far.
cases.why: Past Simple with a period that continues ("so far") is a listed trap.

cases.prompt: Have you been there in 2019?
cases.why: The learner writes the corrected fragment with the subject; it is the same fix as the key ("Were") written differently.

cases.prompt: We have finished two units so far.
cases.why: Over-correction trap: "so far" is an unfinished period, so Present Perfect is correct.

cases.prompt: I ___ here since 2019. (live)
cases.why: Present Perfect Continuous is natural and correct, but the rule describes only have/has + past participle.

cases.prompt: I didn't pay yet.
cases.why: The fix applies the rule (haven't paid); "payed" is a misspelling of "paid", which goes to spellingErrors and does not change the verdict.

cases.prompt: She ___ in London. (work)
cases.why: he/she/it: verb + -s.

cases.prompt: Does he ___ here? (work)
cases.why: After does the main verb has no -s (listed trap).

cases.prompt: It doesn't rain much here.
cases.why: Negative with doesn't + base verb is correct as written.

cases.prompt: She studys at night after work.
cases.why: Spelling of the -s form: studys → studies (listed trap).

cases.prompt: She doesn't work on Sundays.
cases.why: Over-correction trap: after doesn't the verb stays without -s.

cases.prompt: He plays tennis on Saturdays.
cases.why: "ok" is not an accepted shorthand and is not a fix: it may mean "correct as written", so the grader should ask.

cases.prompt: necessary: needed, essential
cases.why: Spelling is graded by code: exact match.

cases.prompt: a place to stay, for example in a hotel
cases.why: Spelling is graded by code: one letter missing.

cases.prompt: the red of a rose
cases.why: Spelling is graded by code: case and outer spaces are ignored.
